title: Riverton's Transport Transformation: A City on the Move
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章和问题中的情景与数据均为模拟教学材料，不是真实调查或官方考试。请根据文章内容选择或填写答案。填空题答案必须来自文章原文，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
A
In 2005, the city of Riverton had a small and simple transport system. Most people travelled by bus or by car. The bus network was limited: there were only twelve bus lines, and buses came every twenty minutes. The city had just one train station, and trains ran only twice a day. Few people used bicycles because there were no cycle lanes. The roads were narrow, and traffic was often slow in the morning and evening. In 2005, the average commute to work took 45 minutes. Many people said the journey was tiring and stressful.

B
By 2025, Riverton had changed a lot. The city now has 36 bus lines, which is three times as many as in 2005. Buses come every eight minutes, so people wait less than before. The train station is bigger, and there are now four train lines. Trains run every fifteen minutes. The city also built 120 kilometres of cycle lanes, and more people ride bicycles to work. The average commute is now 30 minutes. This is 15 minutes shorter than in 2005, and it is one-third less than the old time. The roads are wider, and traffic moves faster. However, the number of cars has increased. In 2005, there were 50,000 cars in the city. Now there are 80,000 cars, which is 1.6 times the old number. This means there are more cars on the road, but the new roads and cycle lanes help to keep traffic moving.

C
The city government spent money on these changes. In 2005, the transport budget was 20 million dollars. In 2025, it is 60 million dollars, which is three times the 2005 budget. The government says the money was well spent because people save time. A survey in 2025 asked 1,000 people about their commute. 70% said they were happy with the transport system, compared with 40% in 2005. The survey also found that 25% of people now cycle to work, while only 5% did in 2005. This is five times the old percentage. However, not everyone is happy. Some drivers say there are too many cars and the roads are still busy at peak times. The government plans to build two more train lines by 2030. It hopes that by then, the average commute will be 25 minutes, which is 5 minutes less than now.

D
Riverton's story shows how a city can change its transport. The number of bus lines has tripled, and the train system has grown. More people cycle, and the average commute is shorter. But the number of cars has also grown, and this brings new challenges. The city will need to balance different types of transport in the future. For example, it must encourage more people to use buses and trains, and it must make cycling safer. The government also wants to reduce pollution. These are big tasks, but Riverton is moving in the right direction.

E
To understand the changes better, let us look at some more numbers. In 2005, the city had only 10 kilometres of cycle lanes. By 2025, this had increased to 120 kilometres, which is twelve times the old length. The number of bus passengers also grew. In 2005, about 5 million people used the bus each year. In 2025, about 15 million people use the bus, which is three times the old number. The train station was small in 2005, with only two platforms. Now it has six platforms, which is three times as many. The city also built a new bridge over the river in 2015. This bridge helped to reduce traffic in the city centre. Before the bridge, cars had to wait a long time at the river crossing. Now they can cross more quickly. The government is proud of these changes, but it knows there is more work to do. It wants to make the city greener and more efficient. For example, it plans to add more electric buses in the next five years. These buses are quieter and cleaner than old buses. The city also wants to build more cycle lanes to connect different parts of the city. This will make cycling safer and more popular. In the future, Riverton hopes to be a model city for sustainable transport.

grammar.title: 倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择
grammar.explanation: 英语中表达倍数常用“times”：three times as many as（是……的三倍多），three times the number（是……的三倍）。比例可用one-third less（少三分之一）、five times the old percentage（是旧百分比的五倍）。比较结构常用“shorter than”“less than”。描述过去数据用一般过去时（was, took, had），描述现在数据用一般现在时（is, has, come）。
grammar.example: The city now has 36 bus lines, which is three times as many as in 2005.
